boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Hofstra rituals and recurring practices, from tulip season and Globe-stage Shakespeare to Pride Court and painted holiday windows.

cards.title: Return to Campus for Fall Festival
cards.subtitle: Hofstra's annual alumni, student, and family weekend
cards.notes: Check the current festival program, then plan around the student expo, carnival, concert, and campus fireworks rather than relying on past schedules.
cards.short_summary: A fall homecoming weekend that brings students, families, and alumni into one Hofstra-wide celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra identifies Fall Festival as an annual university tradition welcoming the entire campus community and as its alumni, student, and family weekend.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the fall; dates, admission rules, and individual event access should be confirmed through Hofstra's current program.

cards.title: See Student Groups Build the Pride Expo
cards.subtitle: Theme-driven booths created for Fall Festival Saturday
cards.notes: Visit the booths during Fall Festival and look for how each organization interprets the student-selected theme while supporting its chosen philanthropy.
cards.short_summary: Student organizations turn a community-voted theme into interactive displays with a charitable component.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra says student organizations construct interactive Pride Expo booths around a theme selected by student social-media voting and raise awareness and funds for philanthropy.
cards.access_notes: Presented on the Saturday of Fall Festival; consult the current festival schedule for location and entry details.

cards.title: Vote Hofstra Royalty onto Pride Court
cards.subtitle: A senior showcase decided by audience ballots
cards.notes: Watch the Friday showcase before the four Hofstra Royalty members are announced Saturday; seniors should review the current candidacy instructions first.
cards.short_summary: Hofstra's homecoming court culminates in four royalty selections determined through audience voting.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra invites seniors to seek annual Pride Court candidacy, holds a Friday showcase, and announces four Hofstra Royalty members from audience votes on Saturday.
cards.access_notes: The showcase typically occurs at 8 p.m. Friday of Fall Festival weekend, with royalty announced Saturday; verify the current schedule.

cards.title: Start the Semester with September Welcome
cards.subtitle: A month-long opening anchored by Welcome Week
cards.notes: Use the month's program to find Welcome Week fireworks, athletics, the Blue and Gold Bash, faculty events, and the concluding Fall Festival.
cards.short_summary: Hofstra stretches its semester opening across September instead of limiting the welcome to move-in week.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra describes September Welcome as a month-long annual program beginning with Welcome Week and ending with Fall Festival.
cards.access_notes: Runs during September; individual activities have separate times, locations, eligibility rules, and possible registration requirements.

cards.title: Gather for Hofstra's September 11 Remembrance
cards.subtitle: The university community's annual memorial service
cards.notes: Look for the year's service notice in Hofstra's official campus communications, then arrive quietly and follow the ceremony's commemorative guidance.
cards.short_summary: An annual Hofstra gathering remembers those killed, saved, and permanently affected by September 11.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra documents a September 11th Remembrance Ceremony held each year and invites all members of the university community to join the service.
cards.access_notes: Annual service details are distributed through official Hofstra communications and Alumni Affairs; confirm the current time and location.

cards.title: Read the Student Center's Painted Holiday Windows
cards.subtitle: Student organizations interpret worldwide observances
cards.notes: Walk the dining-room windows, read each group's interpretation, and join the accompanying crafts without treating distinct holidays as interchangeable.
cards.short_summary: Campus organizations transform Student Center windows into an educational display of celebrations from around the world.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra calls this an annual tradition in which student organizations paint Student Center dining-room windows to interpret holidays celebrated worldwide and create related crafts.
cards.access_notes: The tradition takes place in the Student Center's main dining room; verify current display and reception dates through Hofstra events.

cards.title: Watch Hofstra Turn Dutch Heritage into Tulip Season
cards.subtitle: Tens of thousands of blooms spread across campus each spring
cards.notes: Tour the outdoor plantings in spring and photograph the displays in place; check campus updates because the university gives no exact peak-bloom date.
cards.short_summary: Hofstra marks its Dutch roots through a campus-wide seasonal display of tulips rather than a single monument.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra states that tens of thousands of tulips bloom across campus every spring as a nod to William Hofstra's Dutch heritage.
cards.access_notes: The display is outdoors across campus each spring; Hofstra's page does not specify exact bloom dates or a single viewing site.

cards.title: See Shakespeare on Hofstra's Rebuilt Globe Stage
cards.subtitle: An annual production tradition dating to 1950
cards.notes: Review the season's selected play and performance dates, then confirm whether that production uses Hofstra's historically researched Globe-stage replica.
cards.short_summary: A university festival pairs a changing Shakespeare production with Hofstra's distinctive reconstructed Globe stage.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra says its annual Shakespeare Festival began in 1950 and that the current Globe Stage debuted during the 68th festival in 2017.
cards.access_notes: Productions are staged at scheduled times; consult the current season for dates, ticket requirements, venue, and accessibility information.

cards.title: Mark Graduation with the Senior Class Gift
cards.subtitle: A giving tradition tied to a philanthropy cord
cards.notes: Graduating seniors can review the current campaign before contributing; confirm the stated minimum and cord eligibility for the active class year.
cards.short_summary: Seniors begin their alumni relationship through a class-year donation supporting Hofstra's educational work.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra describes the Senior Class Gift as an enduring tradition supporting undergraduate education; the Class of 2026 minimum gift was $20.26 and qualified donors for a philanthropy cord.
cards.access_notes: Intended for graduating seniors; contribution thresholds and cord eligibility are class-year specific and should be checked before giving.

cards.title: Find Hofstra Stories Engraved in the Walk of Pride
cards.subtitle: Named bricks beside Shuart Stadium and Alumni House
cards.notes: Read the engraved names in Stadium Plaza, or consult Alumni Affairs before ordering a commemorative brick for a student, graduate, or friend.
cards.short_summary: Hofstra supporters leave permanent engraved names in a brick pathway connecting campus memory and philanthropy.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra identifies the Walk of Pride as a special tradition composed of bricks engraved with students', alumni's, and friends' names in Stadium Plaza.
cards.source_title: The Fund for Hofstra University: Alumni and Development
cards.access_notes: The brick walk is in Stadium Plaza near James M. Shuart Stadium and Shapiro Alumni House; ordering a brick requires purchase.
